notes: Inbound SMB lead — small CSaaS startup building chat-first support UI.
Primary complaint: EU end-users see 800-1200ms median TTFB on chat responses; spikes >2s. Frontend devs expect <500ms for initial token stream.
Current setup: using hosted_api default endpoint (region unspecified), client timeout=10s, no streaming enabled in prod. Model: open-weights-variant-1 (latency heavy).
Customer quote: "Customer-facing chat feels sluggish — losing users on first interaction. Can we get sub-500ms?"

SE assessment notes: likely causes = region mismatch (requests routed to us-east), synchronous long prompts (large system/context), no streaming, small client timeout causing retries that exacerbate spikes.
Recommended immediate actions provided in call:
- Switch request region to eu-west for EU traffic (hosted API supports region param) to shave network RTT.
- Enable streaming responses in SDK: send chunked updates to UI so first token arrives fast; target initial-token latency <300-500ms.
- Increase client response timeout to 60s (keep connect timeout 3s) and configure exponential backoff for retries (avoid aggressive retry on perceived timeouts).
- Trim system prompt and reduce context window: move static system/context to prefix cache where possible; keep recent user messages + 1k token context for chat.
- Consider switching to a lower-latency model variant for interactive endpoints (ex: fast-v1) or apply quantized/opt model if available in hosted catalog.
- Use shorter max_tokens for safety and paginate longer responses server-side to control per-request compute.
- Instrument per-request region + model in Console for top routes; add token-level cost + latency dashboard to detect regressions.
Short-term metrics to measure in POC: p50 initial-token latency, p95 full-response latency, token cost per convo, error/retry rate.
Customer is cost-sensitive; requested estimates for moving EU traffic to region vs model changes. Provided quick cost delta doc (drive link).
Open questions: how their CDN and frontend RTTs add to end-to-end numbers; whether they need private networking (likely not — public cloud ok).
Next meeting: 2026-03-05 perf sync to walk through traces and flip eu-west routing for a subset of traffic.
